title: Introduce tenant init timing policy and Helm overlay transformer
author: Lena Park
description: Motivation: On large private installs we still see unpredictable init ordering and a burst of tenant init jobs that competes for control-plane resources. This PR introduces a values-driven "timingPolicy" that lets operators express per-tenant init windows, soft backpressure windows, and jitter profiles, plus a Helm overlayTransformer helper that composes environment-specific overlays (airgap, single-az, high-density) without duplicating templates. The change is intended to be fully backwards compatible: when timingPolicy is omitted, behavior falls back to the current sequenced init job ordering. Work done: - Add values.schema.json extension for timingPolicy and overlayTransformer configuration with validation and examples. - Implement helm/_overlay_transformer.tpl helper and accompanying _init_timing.tpl to materialize ordered CronJobs/Jobs with calculated startDelay annotations. - Add init controller annotation hooks so the private-installer can coordinate with the init-sidecar and migrator when timingPolicy requests soft backpressure. - Introduce small migration patch (post-renderer hook) that backfills legacy init waves into timingPolicy for existing installs opting into the feature. - Update README and chart README sections with examples for airgapped and VPC multi-az deployments, including recommended timingPolicy profiles for low-CPU control planes. Checklist: - [x] values schema and readme examples - [x] templating helpers and unit tests - [x] small migration that is a no-op when feature not enabled - [x] e2e smoke validation in CI (chart test) - [x] documented upgrade notes and rollback guidance Notes: The overlayTransformer is intentionally conservative: it accepts a list of overlay names and a path-based overlay map in values, and composes them deterministically (order of overlays in the list defines precedence). The timingPolicy supports three modes: "sequential" (default), "staggered" (per-tenant window and jitter), and "backpressure" (soft concurrency limit via controller annotations). Related: ENG-4247 (tenant init stability), and a forthcoming small Terraform provider change to expose timingPolicy during private install bootstrapping. Rollout plan: feature gated behind values.enableTimingPolicy=false by default. Operators can opt in per-tenant or cluster-wide. Migration is additive and reversible by clearing timingPolicy values.

review_conversation: Mateo Ruiz (reviewer): Can the overlayTransformer preserve Helm hooks annotations? We rely on post-renderer hooks in some environments.
Lena Park (author): OverlayTransformer preserves annotations and merges hook lists; added a unit test to cover a hook-preservation case.
Riya Singh (reviewer): TimingPolicy looks useful, but we should avoid imposing default jitter that might hide underlying failures. Suggest making jitter opt-in per profile.
Lena Park (author): Good point — changed jitter to default 0ms for sequential and added profile-level jitter field. Updated examples and tests.
Samir Patel (reviewer): CI chart test failed initially on the migration hook flake (post-renderer order). I saw an intermittent where backfill replaced a label. Recommend idempotency re-check.
Lena Park (author): Fixed by making the migration use label-based existence check; re-ran CI and green. Added explicit idempotency assertion in the test.
Mateo Ruiz (approver): Approved — small nit about docs wording on rollback, but not blocking.
Riya Singh (approver): Approved after jitter opt-in change.
Merge: squashed and merged by Lena Park via squash merge.
release_notes: Add optional timingPolicy to private-installer Helm chart for deterministic tenant init windows and a new overlayTransformer helper for composing environment overlays. Feature is opt-in and disabled by default; includes migration helper for existing installs. See docs/private-installer/upgrade-notes.md for migration and rollback guidance.
notes: This PR was intentionally scoped to templating and small migration; it does not change runtime controllers beyond adding opt-in annotations. The companion controller work to implement soft backpressure behavior will be submitted as a follow-up and referenced in ENG-4247.
